data.narrative:
Nominal is a Series B-2 stage AI & Software company seeking valuation support at its current $1B mark, having raised $155M to date. The broader AI & Software sector comprises 11 peer companies across public and private markets, with 1 public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The standard peer-median approach is not applicable here due to insufficient clustering. Despite the 11-company universe in the target's sector, narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) yield fewer than the three minimum datapoints required for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models, maturity, and unit economics within frontier AI. This constraint reflects a fundamental limitation of the comparable-company method for early-stage frontier-tech firms: the population of directly analogous precedents remains thin.

The $1B valuation cannot be validated through traditional triangulation given available data constraints. Resolution would require either (1) expansion of the peer set beyond strict stage and valuation filters, accepting higher methodological risk, or (2) reliance on alternative approaches such as discounted cash flow, venture capital method, or founder-led target multiples. Key uncertainties include the trajectory of Nominal's revenue or user growth, relative to its peers' comparable milestones, and the company's unit economics relative to the broader frontier-AI cohort.
